reviewed_arguments: The HM finite lower-pole model extends to every fixed real tangential order. Both normal tails have the same complete coefficients. Finite real-parameter Taylor remainders and the complementary cone prove every mixed derivative estimate.

Subtracting a sufficiently long model gives an absolutely convergent normal integral. Scaling by the smooth tangential weight proves the full symbol order and every parameter derivative, including tangential dimension zero.

Integrable differences of backward-supported models have continuous inverse kernels vanishing at zero. This proves independence of length and model scale, the alternative-subtraction rule, linearity across declared orders and agreement with absolutely convergent ordinary integrals.

The actual positive-side kernel and every output normal derivative are recovered by dominated integrals. Every binomial factor, normal-frequency power and coefficient derivative is retained. Smooth-input limits agree with the earlier rough-data trace; no uniform same-order symbol convergence is asserted.

The complete tangential product is an absolute shifted-frequency integral after compact-base Fourier decay. The cone split, both restored coefficient tails and every cutoff derivative preserve the full coefficients and remainders with the original tangential factor.

Every original source derivative contributes its exact phase and order. Input distribution transposition has the stated sign. The output trace formula has no artificial restriction from the finite inverse length.

All smooth kernels, separated chart pieces, input-amplitude derivatives, input density and distinct bundle transfers are retained. A normal properness cutoff contributes zero only where it is identically one; arbitrary smoothing contributions are not discarded.

The actual global Cauchy and measurement matrices retain all original boundary orders. Each source-freeze q-part has the proved q-order improvement on the full weighted boundary spaces for every real Sobolev parameter.

The ordered identity comparing two finite inverses retains both error bundles. It proves finite-order independence of the leading weighted trace symbol, without asserting an exact projection or a classical homogeneous expansion.

Four whole examples distinguish the one-sided integral from symmetric principal value, retain an output-coefficient derivative, exhibit the full shifted tangential product with noncommuting matrices, and handle cubic growth and pure polynomials. The plotted curves are labelled samples of exact formulas with open endpoints and the full unplotted tails retained.
